**Scope of this deliverable (as requested):** cross‑walk to the ADR transport class + packing group; set marking / placarding (Class 8 label, UN number, orange plates) and segregation; apply the ADR tunnel restriction code; and HoC‑rank the loading/unloading controls. Sea‑leg (IMDG) detail and rail/air are handled per §6 and the out‑of‑scope flags above.

The 1.1.3.6 partial exemption therefore **does not apply**: full ADR requirements (orange‑plate marking, IBC labelling, driver vocational training per ADR 8.2, prescribed transport equipment, instructions in writing) apply to this consignment.

## 3. Marking, labelling & placarding (ADR road leg)

**Key structural distinction applied:** the goods travel as **IBCs (packaged carriage)**, *not* in a tank or in bulk. Under ADR this changes the plate set — packaged carriage takes **plain, unnumbered orange plates**; numbered plates (hazard identification number over UN number) are for tanks/bulk only.

### 3.1 On each IBC (ADR 5.2 — marking & labelling)

| Marking | Requirement | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| UN number | **"UN 1791"** marked on the IBC | ADR 5.2.1 |
| Hazard label | **Class 8 corrosive label** (model No. 8 — corrosion symbol, white upper / black lower) | ADR 5.2.2 |
| Subsidiary‑risk label | **None** (SDS confirms no subsidiary risk) | SDS §14 |
| Environmentally hazardous substance mark | **Apply** (fish‑and‑tree mark) — marine pollutant, IBC > 5 L. **Confirm** the substance meets the ADR 2.2.9.1.10 aquatic criteria; the SDS marine‑pollutant flag indicates it does. `[ASSUMPTION → confirm from SDS §2/§12]` | ADR 5.2.1.8 |
| IBC design‑type / periodic‑inspection marking | Present (IBCs are "UN‑approved"); **verify each IBC is within its 2.5‑yr / 5‑yr periodic inspection & test date** before loading `[GAP — inspection dates not supplied]` | ADR 6.5.4 |

### 3.2 On the transport unit (ADR 5.3 — placarding & plating)

**Primary case — IBCs carried loose on the road transport unit `[ASSUMPTION — see §10]`:**

- **Two plain orange‑coloured plates (no numbers)**, one at the **front** and one at the **rear** of the transport unit (ADR 5.3.2.1.1). *This is what "orange plates" means for this packaged consignment.*
- **No enlarged Class 8 placards** are required on the vehicle for packaged/IBC carriage.
- **No hazard identification (Kemler) number** is displayed — numbered plates apply only to tank/bulk carriage. A Kemler number is therefore **not assigned here and not invented**.

**Alternative case — IBCs consolidated into a freight container / CTU for the multimodal sea leg:**

- The **container** must be placarded with **Class 8 placards** (enlarged label, min. 250 mm) on **all four sides**, plus the **UN 1791** number and the **marine‑pollutant / environmentally‑hazardous mark** (ADR 5.3.1.2; IMDG 5.3 for the sea leg).
- The road transport unit carrying that container still displays the **orange plates** front and rear.
- **Which case applies is unresolved** — see the tunnel and placarding `[GAP]`s in §10. It materially changes the road‑leg placard set.

## 4. Segregation & mixed loading

**This consignment is a single UN entry (UN 1791 only)** — so no intra‑load mixed‑loading prohibition is triggered within the 12 IBCs, and no ADR 7.5.2 mixed‑loading conflict arises for the consignment as described.

**The controlling incompatibility is chemical, not class‑table:** sodium hypochlorite **reacts with acids to liberate chlorine gas** and reacts violently with reducing agents, ammonia/amines, and many organics. Therefore:

- **Do not co‑load** UN 1791 with **acids** (Class 8 acids), **ammonia/amine solutions**, oxidisable organics, or reducing agents on the same transport unit — or in the same container at the port handover.
- If any other dangerous goods are added to the transport unit or to a consolidated container, apply the **ADR mixed‑loading rules (7.5.2)** for the road leg and the **IMDG segregation table (IMDG 7.2)** for the sea leg **before** the load is built. `[GAP — no other DG declared; re‑assess if the load is consolidated with other consignments at the port]`
- **Keep away from foodstuffs** (general Class 8 handling / hygiene control).
- Load securing and separation to prevent IBC‑to‑IBC abrasion/impact — see §8 (ADR 7.5.7 load securing).

## 5. ADR tunnel restriction — the category‑D tunnel on the route

**The route passes through one ADR category‑D tunnel.** Whether this consignment may transit it depends entirely on the **tunnel restriction code assigned to UN 1791 in ADR Table A, column 15** — a value that has **not been supplied** and that this document **will not invent**.

> ### 🚩 `[GAP]` — ADR tunnel restriction code (Table A, column 15) for UN 1791, PG III, is not supplied.
> This is the single most important open item for routing. **Do not dispatch through the category‑D tunnel until the DGSA (role) resolves this code from the official ADR Table A.**

**Decision rule (once the code is known).** The letter in the ADR tunnel restriction code is the least‑restrictive tunnel category through which passage is **prohibited**; a load is barred from that category and every category "below" it:

| Column‑15 code assigned to the load | May it transit a **Category‑D** tunnel? |
|---|---|
| **B** (incl. B1000C above threshold) | ❌ No — barred from B, C, D and E tunnels |
| **C** (incl. C5000D above threshold) | ❌ No — barred from C, D and E tunnels |
| **D** (incl. D/E) | ❌ No — barred from **D** and E tunnels |
| **E** | ✅ Yes — barred from **E tunnels only** |
| **"—" (no code)** | ✅ Yes — no tunnel restriction |

**So:** the category‑D tunnel is passable **only if** UN 1791's column‑15 code resolves to **E** or **"—"**. If it resolves to **B, C or D**, the tunnel **must not be used** and a **compliant alternative route** is required. The applicable tunnel restriction code must also be entered in the **transport document** (ADR 5.4.1.1.1(k)) and observed against tunnel signage en route (ADR 1.9.5, 8.6).

**Action:** DGSA (role) to resolve the column‑15 code and confirm the routing decision **before dispatch** — see Actions Register (§9), Action A1.

## 6. Multimodal handover (road → sea) — carry‑over and boundary

The class **carries over** at the port, but the sea leg is a **distinct regime (IMDG)** and is **out of the detailed scope** of this ADR deliverable. What is established vs. what must be produced at handover:

**Carries over to IMDG (consistent across modes):** UN 1791 · Class 8 · PG III · marine pollutant.

**Must be resolved against the IMDG Code at the port handover `[GAP — sea‑leg entry not supplied]`:**
- IMDG **EmS emergency schedule** (Fire / Spill) for UN 1791 — do not invent; read from the IMDG DG List.
- IMDG **stowage & segregation** category and any segregation group for the sea leg.
- **Marine‑pollutant mark** on the container/CTU (required for the sea leg).
- **Dangerous Goods manifest / IMO Multimodal Dangerous Goods Form** and, where a container is used, the **Container/Vehicle Packing Certificate**.
- **Segregation from acids/incompatibles** re‑checked on the vessel per IMDG 7.2 (see §4).

The **port handover is itself an unloading/transfer event** — the loading/unloading controls in §8 apply equally to it, coordinated with the **Port DG Coordinator (role)**.

> **Rail (RID) and air (IATA/ICAO‑TI):** out of scope for this deliverable and **not classified here** — flagged, not guessed.

## 8. Loading / unloading controls — hierarchy‑of‑controls ranked

Applies to **both** the origin loading operation **and** the port‑handover unloading/transfer. Each hazard is treated with a higher‑order control first; any lower‑order‑only line is flagged and justified per `KB‑SNIP‑HOC`.

### Hazard 1 — Corrosive contact (skin/eye burns) from leak, splash or coupling failure

| Level | Control | Owner (role) |
|---|---|---|
| **Elimination** | Handle **sealed whole IBCs as unit loads** — **no decanting or open transfer** on the loading dock; this removes the splash/coupling exposure entirely | Loading/Unloading Supervisor (role) |
| **Engineering** | If any transfer is unavoidable, use **dry‑break / closed couplings**; provide **bunded, kerbed loading area with drainage isolated** to contain leaks; site **eyewash + emergency shower** at the loading/transfer point | Consignor (role) / Site Engineering (role) |
| **Administrative** | **Pre‑load integrity check** of each IBC (body, closures, valves, seals, labels/marks intact, periodic‑inspection date valid); spill‑response procedure briefed | Loading/Unloading Supervisor (role) |
| **PPE** *(last line)* | Chemical splash **goggles + face shield**, **corrosion‑resistant gloves** (e.g. nitrile/PVC), chemical apron/suit, chemical‑resistant boots | Loader (role) / Driver (role) |

### Hazard 2 — Chlorine gas release (hypochlorite + acid/contamination/heat → toxic gas)

| Level | Control | Owner (role) |
|---|---|---|
| **Substitution / Elimination** | Eliminate the reaction pathway by **strict segregation from acids and incompatibles** (§4) — never build the load or container with an acid present | DGSA (role) / Loading Supervisor (role) |
| **Engineering** | **Ventilate** any enclosed loading bay / transfer point; provide **chlorine gas detection** where transfer occurs in an enclosed space; keep IBCs **out of direct sun/heat** to limit decomposition | Consignor (role) / Site Engineering (role) |
| **Administrative** | Contamination‑control procedure; gas‑release emergency procedure; evacuation/muster and port notification protocol at handover | Loading/Unloading Supervisor (role) |
| **PPE** *(last line, escalation)* | Appropriate **respiratory protection for chlorine** staged for spill/gas‑release **response only** — **flagged as last‑line: not a substitute for segregation + ventilation + detection above** | Emergency Responder (role) |

### Hazard 3 — IBC drop / mechanical damage / load shift (12 × ~1‑tonne units)

| Level | Control | Owner (role) |
|---|---|---|
| **Engineering** | **Forklift/MHE rated ≥ IBC gross mass** with IBC‑appropriate attachment; **do not double‑stack** in transit unless IBCs are stack‑test rated for it; **rated load‑restraint system** (lashings, anti‑slip mats, headboard) sized to the load | Forklift Operator (role) / Transport Manager (role) |
| **Administrative** | **Load plan & weight distribution**; secure to **ADR 7.5.7** load‑securing; segregate IBCs to prevent abrasion/impact; banksman for MHE movements | Loading/Unloading Supervisor (role) |
| **PPE** *(last line)* | Hi‑vis, safety footwear, head protection in the MHE operating area | All personnel (role) |

### Hazard 4 — Environmental release (marine pollutant) to drains/watercourse

| Level | Control | Owner (role) |
|---|---|---|
| **Engineering** | **Bunded loading/transfer area with isolatable drainage**; spill kit and drain covers staged at loading point and at the port handover | Consignor (role) / Port DG Coordinator (role) |
| **Administrative** | Spill‑containment & notification procedure (marine‑pollutant escalation); confirm bund capacity ≥ largest single IBC (1000 L) | Loading/Unloading Supervisor (role) |
| **PPE** *(last line)* | As Hazard 1 for responders | Emergency Responder (role) |

### Cross‑cutting administrative controls (apply to all hazards)

- **Trained & certificated personnel** — ADR‑trained driver (ADR 8.2); trained loaders/unloaders; DGSA (role) oversight (ADR 1.8.3).
- **Tunnel routing control** — confirm the column‑15 code vs. the category‑D tunnel and plan a compliant route **before dispatch** (§5).
- **SIMOPS / segregation control at the port handover** — coordinate concurrent operations and re‑verify segregation before any consolidation with other DG (§4).
- **Instructions in writing** carried in the cab (ADR 5.4.3); emergency equipment per ADR 8.1.5.

*No hazard above is treated by PPE or administrative measures alone: each carries an elimination/substitution or engineering control ranked ahead of the lower‑order lines.*
